answer: A river monitoring market can view agent claims through a prism of scarce access: issue one nontransferable work ticket per independently metered sensor each day, and pay only for a randomly requested fresh reading. A swarm of aliases shares its sensor ticket, so extra names cannot harvest extra nectar from the reward pool. To scale the attack, an operator must buy and deploy more sensors and maintain real coverage. This does not prove one person per agent; stolen device keys and compromised meter operators can still fabricate access, requiring audits and revocation.
